neighbours.label: The exemplification opener in technical exposition ('For instance,', 'For example,', 'As an example,', 'In this problem') that introduces a worked case right after a general statement
fire: A vector space may have many bases. For instance, in the plane any two non-parallel vectors form one.
Sorting algorithms differ in their worst case. For example, quicksort degrades to quadratic time on sorted input.
Not every ring has unique factorisation. As an example, consider the integers extended by the square root of minus five.
Many functions are not expressible in the simply typed calculus. For instance, the fixed-point combinator has no type.
A graph can be stored in several ways. For example, an adjacency matrix uses quadratic space.
Recursion is not always efficient. In this problem we consider a variant that avoids repeated calls.
Some matrices have no inverse. For instance, any matrix with a zero row is singular.
Closures capture variables by reference. As an example, a loop variable captured in a callback changes after the loop ends.
quiet: A vector space may have many bases, and in the plane any two non-parallel vectors form one.
Sorting algorithms differ in their worst case, and quicksort degrades to quadratic time on sorted input.
Not every ring has unique factorisation; the integers extended by the square root of minus five are the classic case.
Many functions are not expressible in the simply typed calculus. For decades, the fixed-point combinator was the standard illustration.
A graph can be stored in several ways, of which an adjacency matrix is the simplest.
Recursion is not always efficient. In this library we use a variant that avoids repeated calls.
Some matrices have no inverse; any matrix with a zero row is singular.
Closures capture variables by reference. An instance of this class therefore holds a loop variable.
